title: Accenture Technology Vision 2016: People First: The Primacy of People in a Digital Age
notes: Five trends. Labels printed as 'Name: subtitle'; subtitle in note. Published date: PDF created 2016-01-29; first Wayback capture of the PDF 2016-01-25 (trend PDFs) to 2016-02-02. Survey of more than 3,100 executives in 11 countries. Executive summary: 86 percent of executives anticipate the pace of technology change will increase rapidly or at an unprecedented rate in their industry over the next three years. Edition-level forecast: '25% of the world’s economy will be digital by 2020.'

entries.label: Intelligent Automation
entries.quote: Machines and artificial intelligence will be the newest recruits to the workforce, bringing new skills to help people do new jobs, and reinventing what’s possible.
entries.subject: Intelligent automation and AI
entries.note: Edition-level horizon: foreword and Research Methodology say the trends will have 'a profound impact on enterprises for the next three to five years.' Printed subtitle: 'The essential new co-worker for the digital age'. Present-tense survey: 70% of executives are making significantly more investments in AI technologies than they did in 2013.

entries.label: Liquid Workforce
entries.quote: In short, business leaders are realizing their new liquid workforce can become their new competitive advantage.
entries.subject: Adaptive workforce
entries.note: Edition-level horizon: foreword and Research Methodology say the trends will have 'a profound impact on enterprises for the next three to five years.' Printed subtitle: 'Building the workforce for today’s digital demands'.

entries.label: Platform Economy
entries.quote: The unparalleled growth of the digital economy has put it on course to account for 25 percent of the world’s entire economy by 2020, up from 15 percent in 2005.
entries.subject: Platform business models and the digital economy
entries.metric: digital economy share of the world economy
entries.note: Printed subtitle: 'Technology-driven business model innovation from the outside in'. The executive summary calls the 25 percent figure Accenture's own forecast ('we forecast those numbers to increase to 25 percent by 2020').

entries.label: Predictable Disruption
entries.quote: Fast-emerging digital ecosystems—think precision agriculture, the industrial internet or smart cities—create the foundation for the next big wave of enterprise disruption.
entries.subject: Digital ecosystems
entries.note: Edition-level horizon: foreword and Research Methodology say the trends will have 'a profound impact on enterprises for the next three to five years.' Printed subtitle: 'Looking to digital ecosystems for the next waves of change'. Present-tense survey: 82% of executives say industry boundaries are being erased.

entries.label: Digital Trust
entries.quote: Trust is the cornerstone of the digital economy.
entries.subject: Digital trust, security and data ethics
entries.note: Edition-level horizon: foreword and Research Methodology say the trends will have 'a profound impact on enterprises for the next three to five years.' Printed subtitle: 'Strengthening customer relationships through ethics and security'. Survey: 83% agree that trust is the cornerstone of the digital economy.
